summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics). This update records the retained execution for the last-voter removal question: investigation e928fb3f495f4de9a5d56bef8b4c66e0-question-0 now has an interpretation for its own experiment e928fb3f495f4de9a5d56bef8b4c66e0-experiment with conclusion violated, citing receipt 6c7f22d449564006a909a218643cfe08 (completed, exit 0, tests_passed, no parsing errors, 4 parsed events) at decisive parsed indices 0, 1 and 3. Predicate as declared: applying a committed conf change that removes the last voter does not abort the applying node. It is violated at index 1 - the proposal returned no error, the entry was appended at index 2 and committed, and applying it panicked with the changer's own verbatim text 'removed all voters' while the configuration stayed [1] and the node remained StateLeader - with the add-voter control holding at index 3 (applied cleanly, voters [1,2]), which isolates the abort to the change that empties the voter set. The mechanism is traced through sources: the changer rejects an empty voter set only when it computes the result (confchange/confchange.go:170-172, an expected changer-level rejection per its testdata), the propose-time validation never computes that result (raft.go:1318-1335), and applyConfChange converts any changer error into a panic with a TODO to return it to the caller (raft.go:1961-1964). A Fact entry records the instance with its receipt and operands, and the question is marked explained with the sourced Behaviour entry as its premise. Counterevidence is stated plainly - both the changer-level rejection and the apply-time panic are deliberate and documented in the code, the control shows the path otherwise works, and a single-voter cluster is the degenerate case that makes an empty voter set reachable through a legal client proposal - and the limitations record that process-level and restart consequences, larger-cluster variants and the embedding service's own validation duties were not observed, leaving severity and defect classification to human review. No new experiment is requested this turn.
